title: Nearest-neighbor voice conversion and spoof error rates
brief: Convert a voice by averaging each source frame's nearest neighbors in a target speaker's frames, then score a spoofing countermeasure with its false rejection and false acceptance rates and the equal error rate where they cross.
hints: cosine_knn: normalize both sides to unit length, and one matrix product gives every cosine similarity; np.argpartition finds the top k without sorting all of them, then sort only those k.

knn_vc is one line once cosine_knn works: index the matching set with the (T, k) indices and average over the k axis. The query is the source and the keys are the matching set, never the other way around.
error_rates: np.searchsorted(np.sort(scores), thresholds, side="left") counts how many scores fall strictly below each threshold, which gives both error rates for every threshold at once.

equal_error_rate: take every distinct score plus one value above the largest as thresholds, call error_rates, find the first index where frr >= far, and interpolate linearly between it and the index before it.
